observations:
All bechina concepts identified in Torah #97's source text are accommodated within the three proposed packages. No independent domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts was found that would require a fourth package.

THE THREE PACKAGES AND THEIR COVERAGE:

Package 1 — תְּפִלָּה וּמַלְכוּת (Prayer and Kingship) — covers the central teaching: prayer that has the bechina of Malkhut. Eight nodes: תְּפִלָּה, יִרְאָה, מַלְכוּת (core triad, all explicitly bechina-equated in lines 10 and 16), יְהוּדָה (= prayer, line 15), מְחוֹקְקִי (= malkhut/dominion, line 16), מְנַשֶּׁה (= forgetfulness before prayer, line 6), שִׁכְחָה (bechina of Menashe, line 6), אֶפְרַיִם (bechina of transformation during prayer, line 8). These all share the single essential nature of 'sovereign prayer' — prayer conducted with humility and transformation.

Package 2 — שֶׁפַע וְאוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם (Divine Flow and the Letters of the Name) — covers the kabbalistic letter-structure that underlies the teaching. Ten nodes: שֶׁפַע, ה' (אות), חָלָב, א"ל (אותיות), מ"י (אותיות), דָּד, עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת, יוּ"ד (אות), חֶסֶד, אֵל. These share the essential nature of 'divine nurturing flow expressed through the sacred letter-structure of El-Kim/El.'

Package 3 — גִּלְעָד וְהַתַּעֲנוּג הָאֱלֹקִי (Gilad and the Divine Pleasure) — the cosmic/eschatological dimension. Two nodes: גִּלְעָד, תַּעֲנוּג. The bechina pair is: Gilad = gal-ed = the revealed divine pleasure. This package is small (2 nodes) but kept separate rather than merged because the taanug dimension is a distinct ontological domain: it is the reason the world was created (not merely the result of prayer), and its revelation is described as a cosmic event, not merely an inner state of the person praying.

WHY NO FOURTH PACKAGE IS NEEDED:

The three potential alternative structures considered and rejected:

1. Separating Menashe/Efraim into their own package: They form a 2-node and 1-node component respectively. They could be kept separate as 'the two inner conditions of prayer.' However, the Rebbe consistently frames them as two bechinot WITHIN the act of prayer ('כְּשֶׁמִּתְפַּלֵּל בִּשְׁתֵּי בְּחִינוֹת אֵלּוּ' — when praying IN/WITH these two bechinot). They describe the essential character of prayer-with-malkhut, not a separate domain. Merged correctly into Package 1.

2. A separate 'Dalet' (letter-Dalet as withdrawn shefa) package: The Dalet is mentioned once (line 3) as the state when shefa is withdrawn — ה becomes ד. This could have been an evil/neutral 1-node component representing poverty-of-shefa. However: (a) it is not given explicit bechina language ('X הוא בְּחִינַת ד' is absent; the text just says it 'becomes' dalet), (b) it forms no connected component with other bechina-declared nodes, (c) it would be a 1-node component, too small for an independent package. Dalet is the inverse/negative state of the shefa-as-heh concept but not an independently formed bechina domain.

3. A separate 'אֶלְדָּד וּמֵידָד' package: The Rebbe references the heavenly place Eldad-Medad from which shefa descends, but immediately decomposes it into its constituent letter-pairs (א"ל and מ"י). Eldad-Medad is a named source-reference, not independently declared as a bechina concept separate from its constituent letters. Already covered by Package 2.

GOOD/EVIL MIRROR ANALYSIS:

Torah #97 does NOT exhibit the good/evil mirror structure characteristic of many Likutay Moharan Torahs. The teaching is entirely positive — it explains how to achieve prayer-as-malkhut. The negative elements (gadlut as obstacle, machshavot zarot as disruption during prayer, the withdrawal of shefa causing ה to become ד) are presented in the narrative flow (eitza context) rather than as a parallel bechina ontological domain. There is no evil bechina cluster, no 'evil prayer,' no 'evil malkhut' in this Torah's bechina structure.

This is consistent with the Torah's rhetorical purpose: it is a practical teaching for every Jew about how to pray effectively. The evil elements are obstacles to be overcome through the positive teaching, not co-equal ontological domains requiring their own bechina mapping.

CONCLUSION:

Three packages fully account for all 20 bechina-identified concepts in Torah #97. No independent domain of 3+ concepts forming a fourth package was found. Verdict: NO_NEW_PACKAGES.
